question.text: What is the relationship between Authorised Capital, Issued Capital, and Paid-up Capital of a company?

answer.text: Issued Capital ≥ Authorised Capital ≥ Paid-up Capital
Paid-up Capital ≥ Issued Capital ≥ Authorised Capital
Authorised Capital ≥ Issued Capital ≥ Paid-up Capital
All three are always equal for a listed company

explanation.text: The Logic: Authorised Capital is the maximum capital a company can raise as per its Memorandum of Association. Issued Capital is the portion actually offered to investors, which cannot exceed Authorised Capital. Paid-up Capital is the amount actually received from shareholders, which cannot exceed Issued Capital. Hence: Authorised ≥ Issued ≥ Paid-up. The Trap: Option D is wrong because these three need not be equal — a company may not issue all its authorised capital, and shareholders may not pay up all issued capital (partly paid shares).
